Hi Alex — thanks for the quick note. A few practical details from the engineering side to help your security team triage:

- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II (Security + Availability) as of 2026-04-01. We maintain continuous monitoring on key infra controls and run quarterly control reviews; the full report can be shared under NDA.

- HIPAA / BAA: We offer a standard BAA for customers handling PHI. Backups are covered under the BAA terms.

- Deletion SLAs (summary):
  • Primary storage: user-initiated deletion results in immediate logical deletion and removal from live indexes; objects are marked for purge and are typically purged from primary storage within 24 hours.
  • Backups / snapshots: incremental snapshots are retained for 30 days by default; permanently purged from backup storage within 35 days of deletion request (30-day retention window + up to 5-day retention purge window to account for snapshot lifecycle).
  • Long-term archival: we do not move production data into immutable long-term archives by default; if a customer requests exports/archives for compliance, those are explicitly managed and documented in the contract.

- Logs: access and audit logs are retained in hot storage for 90 days, then moved to cold/archival logs for up to 365 days depending on the customer contract. Log deletion for a data subject request: audit logs are redacted for user-identifying fields where feasible; full deletion of all audit records tied to a subject may have limitations for regulatory/forensic reasons — we can scope exact expectations with your legal team.

I’ve attached a CSV that lays out the retention windows and the default SLA buckets (Redwood_Data_Retention_Table.csv). Also linking the VSQ URL: https://redwood.app/questionnaire/AMAYA-VDQ-001

If you want, I can coordinate a short 30-minute session with Neha (security) for any deep-dive on backups and encryption-at-rest key rotation.

Thanks,

Hi Alex / Sarah —

Following up with formal answers and a few policy clarifications so your security and legal teams have something to review:

1) SOC 2: as Rishi noted, current SOC 2 Type II report is 2026-04-01 (Security & Availability). We can share the full report under NDA along with our control matrix. We also publish quarterly control health dashboards to customers.

2) HIPAA / BAA: Redwood offers a standard BAA. Backups are included in the BAA scope. We recommend routing the BAA through your legal and we’ll provide a standard template.

3) Data deletion / retention (definitive):
  - Live data: upon request Redwood initiates logical deletion immediately and triggers index removal. Default SLA: 24 hours for logical purge from live clusters.
  - Backups / snapshots: default snapshot retention is 30 days. After a deletion request, objects are excluded from new snapshots immediately; existing snapshots containing that object are kept for the remainder of the 30-day snapshot window. We guarantee permanent removal from backup storage within 35 days of the deletion request.
  - Immutable archives: we do not archive production data into immutable cold storage without explicit customer instruction. If you require longer archives, we will document retention/termination obligations in the contract.

4) Log retention and deletion:
  - Access/audit logs: hot storage retention 90 days, cold/archival up to 365 days (default), configurable per contract.
  - Deletion requests for logs: we can redact user-identifying information from logs where possible; full deletion of logs may be constrained by security forensic needs and regulatory requirements — we’ll work with Legal to define what can be redacted vs retained.

5) Encryption & keys: all customer data at rest is encrypted; customers on Dedicated/Private can bring their own KMS keys (BYOK) and we support periodic key rotation. Backups are encrypted with the same key policy as the primary environment.

Next steps we recommend:
- Please have your security team complete the attached VSQ and upload to the link Rishi shared.
- If Amaya needs a formal BAA or NDA first, confirm and we’ll route the templates.
- If you want a technical deep-dive on backup lifecycle or a runbook for deletion cases, we can schedule a 30–45 minute session with our security engineering team (I can host).

Happy to jump on a call this week if helpful.

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
